title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
authors: E. Fugl, L. L. Olsen, S. Sasmal, M. Efthymiou-Tsironi, G. Nagda, F. Krizek, L. Casparis, S. Vaitiekėnas
abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches $h/4e^2$, consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.
summary: This work reports on the continuous electrostatic tuning of quantum critical behavior in Josephson junction arrays, accessing superconducting, insulating, and metallic states. By analyzing the evolution of critical resistivity and scaling exponents, the authors demonstrate a unified picture connecting different quantum phase transitions. This provides a highly controllable platform for testing fundamental theories of quantum criticality.
main_problem: The study investigates the continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior across superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes within a single device.
main_result: The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously as the system is tuned by dual electrostatic gates, connecting previously disparate superconducting transition regimes.
method: The researchers employed finite-temperature scaling analysis of resistivity isotherms and measured magnetoresistance to characterize the quantum phase transitions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid Josephson junction array (JJA) built on an InAs 2DEG, allowing independent control over interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity using dual top and frame gates.
key_observables: Critical resistivity ($ho_C$), scaling exponent ($\alpha$), and magnetoresistivity ($ho(B)$).
important_parameters: Cooper-pair resistance quantum ($ho_Q = h/4e^2$), quantum-percolation estimate, and gate voltages ($V_{FG}, V_{TG}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on scaling theory for the Superconductor-Insulator Transition (SIT) and uses dirty-limit approximations for magnetotransport analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure, the phase diagram showing the three transport regimes, and temperature-dependent resistivity traces used for scaling analysis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by varying gate voltages, analyzing the temperature dependence of resistivity to extract critical exponents, and characterizing the crossover between different quantum regimes.
why_interesting: The ability to tune quantum critical points continuously using electrostatic gates provides a clean experimental platform to test universal scaling theories applicable to various quantum many-body systems.
